pull.title: qa: Fix `interface_ipc*.py` on NetBSD and prevent future regressions
pull.body:
This PR fixes the `interface_ipc*.py` tests, which have been [failing](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35037#issuecomment-6082043240) on NetBSD since https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35037.

As file descriptor budget regressions of this kind recur (see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31537 and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36078), the macOS CI job now models NetBSD's limit so they are caught before merging rather than by nightly NetBSD CI afterwards.

See the commit messages for details.

qa: Account for `-ipcbind` file descriptors in `-maxconnections`

Since `-ipcbind` reserves one listening socket plus
`ipc::DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS` (16) client slots in `min_required_fds`,
the framework's `-maxconnections=76` no longer fits the 256 file
descriptor budget on NetBSD, and every `interface_ipc*.py` node starts
with "Warning: Reducing -maxconnections ...", which the framework treats
as a failure.

Lower `-maxconnections` by that reservation on IPC-enabled nodes only,
so the rest of the suite keeps its P2P connection slots.

ci: Enforce NetBSD's 256 file descriptor budget in the macOS job

On select()-based platforms such as NetBSD, `bitcoind` can use at most
`FD_SETSIZE` (256) file descriptors, so the functional test framework
pins `-maxconnections` to that budget. Any change that grows
`min_required_fds` then makes every node print "Warning: Reducing
-maxconnections ...", which the framework treats as a failure. Such
regressions are currently caught only by nightly NetBSD CI (see #31537,

Add a `CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT` knob that runs functional test node processes
through a wrapper capping `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, and enable it for the macOS
native job with NetBSD's value of 256.

events.body: NetBSD test logs are available here: https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/39563835829.

Concept ACK

But `wrap-fd-limit.sh‎` in 311bc7c3bb274c7065f871198fa0910c205b8a6a loses our coverage for "infinite" file descriptors introduced by #34937.

We could run `feature_init.py` both capped and uncapped:

```diff
diff --git a/ci/test/03_test_script.sh b/ci/test/03_test_script.sh
index d5981147f4..1468638690 100755
--- a/ci/test/03_test_script.sh
+++ b/ci/test/03_test_script.sh
@@ -161,5 +161,6 @@ if [ -n "${CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT}" ]; then
   # Only the node processes are capped (via BITCOIN_CMD), not the Python
   # test runner, which needs more descriptors when running jobs in parallel.
-  export BITCOIN_CMD="${BASE_ROOT_DIR}/ci/test/wrap-fd-limit.sh ${BITCOIN_CMD:-bitcoin}"
+  BITCOIN_CMD_UNCAPPED="${BITCOIN_CMD:-bitcoin}"
+  export BITCOIN_CMD="${BASE_ROOT_DIR}/ci/test/wrap-fd-limit.sh ${BITCOIN_CMD_UNCAPPED}"
 fi
 
@@ -208,4 +209,20 @@ if [ "$RUN_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS" = "true" ]; then
     --quiet \
     --failfast
+
+  if [ -n "${CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT}" ]; then
+    # The capped suite also runs feature_init.py, but the wrapper overrides the
+    # RLIM_INFINITY and above-INT_MAX limits it tests. Repeat it without the cap.
+    BITCOIN_CMD="${BITCOIN_CMD_UNCAPPED}" \
+    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${DEPENDS_DIR}/${HOST}/lib" \
+    "${BASE_BUILD_DIR}/test/functional/test_runner.py" \
+      "${MAKEJOBS}" \
+      --tmpdirprefix "${BASE_SCRATCH_DIR}/test_runner_uncapped/" \
+      --ansi \
+      --combinedlogslen=99999999 \
+      --timeout-factor="${TEST_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_FACTOR}" \
+      --quiet \
+      --failfast \
+      feature_init.py
+  fi
 fi
```

Alternatively we could drop that test.

@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+#
+# Copyright (c) The Bitcoin Core developers
+# Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying
+# file COPYING or https://opensource.org/license/mit/.
+#
+# Run a command with RLIMIT_NOFILE capped at $CI_LIMIT_FD_COUNT.
+#
+# On select()-based platforms such as NetBSD, bitcoind can use at most
+# FD_SETSIZE (256) file descriptors regardless of the RLIMIT_NOFILE. Capping the
+# hard limit here makes RaiseFileDescriptorLimit() return the same number on any
+# platform, so an fd-budget regression (e.g. a new "Reducing -maxconnections ..."
+# warning on stderr, which the functional test framework treats as a failure) is
+# caught by this job instead of only on NetBSD.
+
+export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
+set -o errexit
